analysis.title: DB CoTD: 337 UP!
key_insights: Yesterday 337 S&P 500 stocks rose but the index fell -1.21%, the second-worst S&P 500 performance across the 2,887 days since October 1996 on which more than 300 stocks advanced.

The only worse 300+ advancer day was 27 January 2025, when the index fell -1.46% with 351 stocks up. That was the DeepSeek day, when assumptions about the need for costly AI capex were challenged and NVIDIA fell -17%.
US AI capex has been questioned repeatedly in the 21 months since DeepSeek. From the day before DeepSeek, NVIDIA is still up nearly +50% and the Bloomberg Global AI index is up a similar amount.
NVIDIA is only +2.5% since 29 October 2025, the date of Meta's results when its capex plans were seriously questioned and AI market leadership changed.
Deutsche Bank frames the last 12 months as AI leadership shifting from those writing the cheques (capex spenders) to those cashing them (suppliers).
The Global AI index is up around +17% over that period, but outside NVIDIA's flat performance, other large US AI companies are lower: Oracle -53.3%, Broadcom -15.6%, Meta -13.4%, Microsoft -3.0%.

The open question is whether yesterday's drop is another temporary wobble in the AI capex story or whether the market is starting to believe the size of the capex cheques matters more than what they buy.
Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon all report next week, which DB flags as a big week for the AI capex story.
earnings_insights: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are all scheduled to report results next week. DB flags these as a test of the AI capex story. No estimates are given in the note.
risk_factors: Renewed doubt about the return on US AI capex, with the size of spending judged to matter more than what it buys.
Next week's Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon results could reinforce or ease concerns about AI capex.
charts_described: Today's CoTD chart shows S&P 500 advancer counts against index performance, with yesterday at 337 advancers and a -1.21% index move among days with more than 300 advancers.
vol_and_positioning: Breadth was strong while the index fell: 337 S&P 500 stocks advanced yet the index lost -1.21%, which points to heavy losses in the largest index weights. Only one 300+ advancer day was worse (27 January 2025, -1.46% with 351 advancers).

tension_points.bull_case: The AI trade has held up over the long run: NVIDIA is up nearly +50% and the Bloomberg Global AI index is up a similar amount since the day before DeepSeek, despite repeated questioning of US AI capex. Yesterday's drop could be another temporary wobble.
tension_points.bear_case: Leadership has shifted from the capex spenders to the suppliers. Since 29 October 2025 NVIDIA is only +2.5% and Oracle (-53.3%), Broadcom (-15.6%), Meta (-13.4%) and Microsoft (-3.0%) are lower. The market may now be judging that the size of the cheques matters more than what they buy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon results are flagged as the test for the AI capex story.

theme_stances.key_argument: Yesterday's broad participation but sharply lower index raises the question of whether the market now believes the size of AI capex cheques matters more than what they buy.
theme_stances.evidence: size of the cheques matters more than the promise of what they will buy
